query: Consider the following context: The combination of elevated temperature and tribo-corrosion leads to the accelerated degradation of structural components used in many extreme environments. Recently developed high-entropy alloys (HEAs) with multiple principal elements have the potential for superior degradation resistance compared with presently used structural alloys. In that context, which material can be used for superior tribo-corrosion degradation resistance, and why?

generation.hypothesis: The dual‐phase eutectic high‐entropy alloy AlCoCrFeNi2.1 exhibits superior tribo-corrosion degradation resistance relative to conventional alloys (e.g., DS2205 stainless steel) under high-temperature, corrosive conditions because its unique microstructure promotes the formation of a protective barrier that slows down oxidation and selective dissolution of the less‐noble phase.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast, dual-phase microstructure consisting of a body-centered cubic (BCC/B2) phase and a face-centered cubic (FCC/L12) phase with enrichment of noble elements on the FCC phase surface.
generation.intervention: Exposure to high-temperature tribo-corrosive conditions, specifically in molten salt environments (e.g., NaCl-KCl-MgCl2) at temperatures such as 450 °C and 650 °C combined with mechanical (sliding) stresses.
generation.conditions: High-temperature molten salt corrosive environment with simultaneous mechanical wear (tribo-corrosion), similar to conditions in concentrating solar power systems.
generation.structural_mediator: The dual-phase microstructure leads to micro-galvanic coupling where selective dissolution of the less noble phase occurs, while the FCC phase acts as a barrier via enrichment of noble elements and an increased work function, thereby reducing further oxidation.
generation.mechanism: The barrier mechanism is mediated by the protective FCC phase that forms on the surface upon elevated temperature exposure. This phase increases the work function at higher temperatures, inhibiting further oxidation and corrosion propagation, along with reducing the detrimental effects of micro-galvanic coupling under tribo-corrosion conditions.
generation.predicted_outcome: A significantly lower tribo-corrosion degradation rate (lower corrosion and wear depth) compared to conventional alloys such as DS2205 under identical high-temperature molten salt and mechanical wear conditions.
generation.baseline: Performance of conventional duplex stainless steel 2205 (DS2205) under similar high-temperature molten salt and wear conditions, which shows higher degradation rates.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is confined to high-temperature, molten salt environments where both corrosion and mechanical wear act concurrently. Its validity outside such environments (e.g., non-molten salt or lower temperature conditions) remains uncertain.
generation.uncertainty: While evidence supports improved molten salt corrosion performance, the precise interaction between tribological wear and corrosion (tribo-corrosion) and its long-term impact on the alloy's protective mechanism require further experimental validation.

falsification_experiment.design: Conduct an accelerated tribo-corrosion test by subjecting samples of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 and DS2205 to sliding wear in molten NaCl-KCl-MgCl2 salt at 450 °C and 650 °C. Use identical mechanical loads and exposure durations for both materials.
measurements: Corrosion rate (mm/year) via weight loss measurement
Wear track depth and width using profilometry
Surface phase composition using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX)
Work function or potential mapping via scanning kelvin probe microscopy
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If AlCoCrFeNi2.1 does not show a statistically significant lower corrosion rate and reduced wear compared to DS2205, or if no evidence is observed for a protective barrier (such as an increased work function related to the FCC phase) after testing, the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Abstract Dual-phase high entropy alloys have recently attracted widespread attention as advanced structural materials due to their unique microstructure, excellent mechanical properties, and corrosion resistance. However, their molten salt corrosion behavior has not been reported, which is critical in evaluating their application merit in the areas of concentrating solar power and nuclear energy. Here, the molten salt corrosion behavior of AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy (EHEA) was evaluated in molten NaCl-KCl-MgCl 2 salt at 450 °C and 650 °C in comparison to conventional duplex stainless steel 2205 (DS2205). The EHEA showed a significantly lower corrosion rate of ~1 mm/year at 450 °C compared to ~8 mm/year for DS2205. Similarly, EHEA showed a lower corrosion rate of ~9 mm/year at 650 °C compared to ~20 mm/year for DS2205. There was selective dissolution of the body-centered cubic phase in both the alloys, B2 in AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 and α-Ferrite in DS2205. This was attributed to micro-galvanic coupling between the two phases in each alloy that was measured in terms of Volta potential difference using a scanning kelvin probe.
